articles.title: 'US Midterm elections tend to be referendums on the unpopularity of the president'
articles.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Michelle Swers, Professor of Government at Georgetown University. She frames the New Hampshire primary as both a major Senate contest and an unusually strong indication of the national political climate ahead of November. While Democrats face a difficult Senate map and cannot afford to surrender an open seat they already hold, the broader midterm political environment might become a referendum on President Donald Trump’s performance. articles.title: Saxony-Anhalt poll: 'A huge blow for the CDU, but also a huge win for the AfD'
articles.description: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Markus Ziener, Visiting Senior Fellow at the German Marshall Fund. He interprets the AfD’s breakthrough in Saxony-Anhalt as a potentially historic turning point in post-war German politics. For Ziener, the significance lies not only in the scale of the far right’s electoral success, but also in the constituency behind it: many AfD voters, he argues, were previously politically disengaged rather than simply defecting from established parties. This complicates conventional explanations of the result as a straightforward transfer of support from the CDU to the AfD and raises a deeper question about the political expectations of a newly mobilised electorate. At the same time, Ziener draws an important distinction between electoral strength and governing capacity. Saxony-Anhalt’s limited powers mean that even an AfD-led government could struggle to fulfil major promises on migration, Ukraine and other national policy questions. The immediate consequences may therefore be felt most strongly elsewhere: in the destabilisation of the established parties and, particularly, in mounting pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz. Ziener portrays the result as a challenge reaching “to the core of his chancellorship,” with further regional elections threatening to turn a state-level defeat into a broader test of Germany’s political direction.

articles.description: The move completes a shake-up of Kemi Badenoch's top team ahead of the party's conference in October.

articles.title: Netanyahu's wife shares conspiracy claim that opposition leader knew of Oct 7 attacks in advance
articles.description: As Israel prepares for what are expected to be close-fought parliamentary elections in October, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's wife Sara on Monday shared a conspiracy theory that centre-left opposition figure Yair Golan had advance warning of the Hamas-led October 7, 2023 attacks.

articles.title: Former gang member found guilty of murdering rapper Tupac Shakur
articles.description: A jury found Duane “Keffe D” Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 killing of rap icon Tupac Shakur, finally bringing a measure of resolution to a case that had gripped hip-hop fans and lingered in the public imagination for decades. Davis could be sentenced to life in prison following that verdict. FRANCE 24's Wassim Cornet tells us more about the verdict.

articles.title: Baby Tommy's our 'light', says grieving family of newborn whose mum died in childbirth
articles.description: Chelsea McGillivray, from Rutherglen, South Lanarkshire, fell into cardiac arrest during labour after what was believed to be a textbook pregnancy.

articles.title: Tibetan activists accuse China of underreporting flood death toll
articles.description: Tibetan exiles and activists have accused China of severely underreporting the death toll from the devastating Himalayan floods along its border with Nepal. Beijing has reported 16 deaths and 546 missing in Tibet so far and the foreign ministry insists that the release of information has been "open, transparent and timely".

articles.title: 'Glaciers in Himalayas retreating': Nepal floods triggered by 'glacier collapse & massive landslide'
articles.description: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Joseph Shea, Glaciologist and Associate Professor at the University of Northern BC. Shea argues that the catastrophe should be understood as a compound event in which a glacier failure and a massive landslide occurred together. His analysis places the disaster within the broader, well-established transformation of the Himalayas under climate change. As warming changes high-mountain environments, scientists may increasingly need to identify subtle precursors to rare but potentially devastating cascading hazards.

articles.title: Government air strikes kill 20 alleged guerrillas in Colombia, president says
articles.description: Fresh government air strikes have killed 20 alleged members of the Central General Staff (EMC) armed group in southern Colombia, the country's new right-wing President Abelardo de la Espriella said Monday. The new administration carried out two other deadly air strikes against suspected guerrillas in August, which sources within Colombia's forensics authority say killed at least four minors.

articles.title: 'I'm on a mission to convince people to work less'
articles.description: Jo Hooper spent her 20s chasing career success, but had two work-related breakdowns before she was 31.

articles.title: 'She was trying to get better' - the lives lost to drug overdoses
articles.description: Jenna McCune's family was among relatives remembering loved ones they lost through drug overdoses.

articles.title: 'Sea change: Much of the world's economic GDP has moved to the Asia-Pacific region'
articles.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Rana Mitter, historian, author and ST Lee Chair in US-Asia Relations at the Harvard Kennedy School. He discusses the significance of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) as it pertains to the evolution of a changing international system, this as the bloc holds a summit in Kyrgyzstan's capital Bishkek.

articles.title: Kilian, Jade and Miriam - meet the people sharing their names with storms
articles.description: The list of 21 names has been announced by the Met Office, Met Éireann and the Dutch weather service and comes into effect on 1 September.

articles.title: We survived the Aberfan disaster as schoolchildren, but were told to never talk about it again
articles.description: In one of Britain's worst disasters, 116 children were killed on the morning of 21 October 1966.

articles.title: US military striking targets in Iran after attempted attacks on shipping
articles.description: The US military said on Tuesday it is striking new targets in Iran as hostilities flare again after a month without military action. US Central Command said that the strikes follow recent attempted attacks by the Iranian government against commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. Follow our liveblog to see how the day's events unfolded.

articles.title: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis found guilty in Tupac Shakur murder
articles.description: Duane “Keffe D” Davis was found guilty Monday of orchestrating the 1996 murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur, becoming the first person convicted in the decades-old case. The 63-year-old faces a possible life sentence after a Las Vegas jury deliberated for less than three hours.

articles.title: Melting Himalayas? Nepal disaster exposes growing risk of glacial flooding
articles.description: It may well be one of the tragic consequences of global warming. Scientists will tell us whether receding glaciers are to blame for last Wednesday’s ice shelf collapse that triggered a catastrophic flood, cascading down more than 3,000 metres from the Chinese border into Nepal.

articles.title: Nepal-Tibet flood death toll surpasses 1,000
articles.description: Rescuers battled mud and debris Monday as the death toll from devastating glacial floods along the China-Nepal border topped 1,000, with nearly 4,500 people still missing. Rescue teams continued a desperate search for survivors as entire communities were swept away.

articles.title: Trump threatens to ‘hit Iran hard’ as strikes resume after month-long lull
articles.description: President Donald Trump said Monday that the US would hit back against Iranian attacks on US targets in the Middle East, according to a Fox News reporter. The Iranian attacks were themselves a response to US strikes on an island in the Strait of Hormuz, the first flare-up in a month.

articles.title: Kenyan airport staff strike delays thousands of passengers
articles.description: In tonight's edition: A workers' strike at Kenya's main airport leaves travellers grounded. Also, Ghanaian cocoa farmers are ramping up their pushback against a new law preventing them from using their land for anything else without permission. And in Tunisia, the picturesque town of Sidi Bou Saïd has been recognised by UNESCO as being important to global heritage.

articles.title: Nepal disaster: Fake and AI images flood social media as deaths mount
articles.description: As deadly floods hit the Nepal-China border, social media is being inundated with fake and misleading footage. In Truth or Fake, Vedika Bahl goes through viral videos falsely linked to the disaster, including AI-generated content and old recycled footage from India, Chile and Alaska. Some posts have racked up millions of views online, exploiting the tragedy to drive engagement for easy clicks or further perpetuate conspiracy theories.

articles.title: Trump vows to hit back 'hard' after first exchange of fire with Iran in weeks
articles.description: Donald Trump threatened to hit Iran "hard" after the two foes traded fire for the first time in over a month, while Iran's president warned that more fighting with the US was not in his country's interest. After six months of war, the foes remain at an impasse, with Iran keeping the strategic Strait of Hormuz closed and the US persisting with a naval counter-blockade of Iran. FRANCE 24's Reza Sayah reports from Tehran.

articles.title: Hundreds feared stuck in hydropower tunnels as flood deaths surpass 950 in Nepal and China
articles.description: Rescuers raced Monday to free hundreds of workers believed to be trapped in tunnels at hydropower sites that were buried in mud by catastrophic flooding on the Nepal-China border, as the death toll climbed and increasingly desperate families searched for missing loved ones. FRANCE 24's Eliza Herbert reports.

articles.title: Raising the Altalena: Netanyahu digs up sunken 1948 arms ship in ‘pre-election stunt’
articles.description: A ship carrying arms for a right-wing militia, the Altalena was sunk 78 years ago off the coast of Tel Aviv at the orders of Israel’s founders. The discovery of its wreckage last week has given the country’s right-wing government ammunition to target the left and attempt to redirect the campaign for legislative elections in October.

articles.title: France targets Shein and Temu with new fast fashion levy
articles.description: Starting this week, France will charge a penalty on cheaply made clothing sold by ultra-fast fashion retailers, with the fee reaching nearly €20 per item by 2030. Aimed at platforms like Shein, Temu and AliExpress, the levy follows a June law targeting disposable fashion's environmental toll, though rival brands like H&M and Zara are exempt.

articles.title: Nepal floods 'unprecedented', requires new 'engineering approaches, risk-sensitive urban planning'
articles.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Dr. Basanta Raj Adhikari, Director of the Center for Disaster Studies at Tribhuvan University’s Institute of Engineering. He describes the disaster as an illustration of the limits of conventional prevention in the Himalayas. With flood velocities estimated at 170 to 180 kilometres per hour and hazards ranging from ice and snow avalanches to glacial lake outburst floods, he argues that comprehensive monitoring of Nepal’s exceptionally steep and complex mountain terrain is effectively impossible. Yet Adhikari’s analysis is not fatalistic. Instead, he shifts the emphasis from attempting to predict every extreme event toward risk-informed adaptation. Nepal, he argues, should identify high-risk hotspots through satellite observation, supplement these with ground-based monitoring and early-warning systems, and incorporate that knowledge into risk-sensitive land-use planning.

articles.title: Watch: Notting Hill Carnival celebrates 60th anniversary
articles.description: The three-day event saw dancers in extravagant outfits parading the streets of west London to celebrate Caribbean arts and culture.

articles.title: Latest flare-up between US and Iran bring conflict's lull to an end
articles.description: Iran's foreign minister has accused Israel's Benjamin Netanyahu of tricking the United States into war with the Islamic Republic. Over six months into the conflict, there appears to be no end in sight. This after the US struck sites in Iran, prompting Tehran to respond. An April ceasefire brought an end to intense fighting, but sporadic attacks have continued over the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran's closure of the waterway during the conflict has pressured global oil markets, and in turn Donald Trump at home.

articles.title: Canberra's zoo treats its residents to personnalised musical therapy
articles.description: A music therapist in Australia has been playing for animals at Canberra's zoo for the last five years. It's a relaxing experience for animals and staff alike and the animals all react differently to the music played.

articles.title: Nepal deadly floods: FRANCE 24 report – on the ground with survivors
articles.description: In Nepal, after the deadly flood, another ordeal begins for the survivors: finding shelter, food, and simply the means to survive. While rescue workers continue searching for possible survivors, those who escaped the disaster are trying to rebuild their lives, despite the threat of another flood. FRANCE 24's special correspondents visited Sinchaur in the Nuwako district – one of the villages hit by the flood on August 26.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz accessibility at the centre of US-Iran war flare-up
articles.description: For the first time in a month, the US has launched strikes against Iran. The attack targeted the shipping island of Larak in the Strait of Hormuz. The US says it was aimed at preventing Tehran from placing sea mines in the strategic shipping lane, just days after Washington announced it had completed clearing explosives from there. Iran then reiterated its attacks, saying it had struck two US military bases in Jordan. FRANCE 24's Rochelle Ferguson-Bouyahi tells us more.

articles.title: Business groups urge Swinney to scrap 'ineffective' food price cap plan

articles.title: Relentless heat worsens Gaza's ongoing struggle to access water
articles.description: In Gaza, securing drinking water is a relentless daily struggle. The war with Israel has destroyed critical water and sanitation infrastructure, and as temperatures soar, the extreme heat is escalating an already severe shortage into a deadly humanitarian crisis. Two and a half years of war with Israel have damaged or destroyed nearly 90% of Gaza’s water and sanitation infrastructure according to UNICEF.

articles.title: Iran, US trade fire in first exchange in a month
